title: 登高
author: Du Fu

translation: the wind is sharp, the sky is high, gibbons wail mournfully
the islet is clear, the sand is white, birds circle back
leaves fall without end from the boundless woods
the endless long river rolls on toward him
ten thousand miles from home, i grieve in autumn and live as a guest
in a life of a hundred years and many illnesses, i climb this terrace alone
hardship and bitter regret have frosted my temples
down and out, i have just given up my cup of cloudy wine

appreciation: Du Fu stands alone on a high terrace in late autumn, while wind, gibbons, falling leaves, and the endless Yangtze press in from every direction. The landscape is vast and the human figure is small, sick, and far from home. The poem matters because its strict parallel couplets hold all that grief in perfect form, and it is often called the greatest regulated verse in Chinese.
